compositionRules.assert: For any filtering or list-view UI, prefer antd.select over a free-text antd.input to constrain the answer set.
compositionRules.condition: intent == filtering or root is list/table toolbar

compositionRules.assert: Render antd.select inside antd.form.Item (not bare) so the selected value participates in form validation and submission.

bad: <Select options={[{label:'All',value:'all'},{label:'Active',value:'active'}]} placeholder="Filter by status" mode="multiple" />  // multi-value filtering
<Select options={users.map(u=>({label:u.name,value:u.id}))} placeholder="Select assignee" />  // enum of dynamic options
good: <Select options={[]} />  // MISSING placeholder: user sees an empty control with no guidance

hardRules.message: Select requires options as an array of option objects (each {label,value}); without options the dropdown has nothing to choose and is invalid for data_entry.
When options are provided, a placeholder must be supplied to communicate the field's purpose before a value is chosen.
value arity must match mode: multiple/tags require an array value; default (single) mode requires a scalar value.

hardRules.expr: exists(opt in props.options where opt.value == props.value) OR props.value == null OR props.mode in ['multiple','tags']
hardRules.message: In single-select mode the selected value must correspond to one of the provided options (or be empty); out-of-range values are invalid.
Select border and background must bind to the named input tokens (input.border.color, input.background), not raw or placeholder colors.

meaning.definition: Lets the user commit a single choice (or a bounded set of choices) from a finite, enumerated domain — turning an open-ended question into a constrained, machine-resolvable answer. In a filtering context it narrows a dataset to the rows matching the chosen value(s).
doNotUseWhen: The answer space is effectively unbounded or free-form (use antd.input instead).
There are only two mutually-exclusive states (use antd.switch).
The choice triggers an immediate primary action rather than recording a value (use antd.button).
The available options depend on heavy server-side search across a huge set (consider a dedicated search component).
useWhen: The user must pick one value from a known, finite list of options.
A form field has a constrained enum domain (status, category, assignee).
A list or table needs a filter control that reduces rows by an enumerated attribute.
Multi-select of tags or multiple items is required (mode multiple/tags).

contentRules: Each item SHOULD carry both a human-readable label and a stable value.
value fields must be unique within the array.
Avoid embedding raw markup in label; prefer plain text.
options.description: Array of option objects to populate the dropdown. Each option typically exposes at least { label, value }; extra fields drive filtering and rendering.

value.description: Currently selected option value. Scalar for default single-select mode; array when mode is multiple or tags.

mode.description: Selects the selection semantics. Omit (or unset) for single-choice; 'multiple' for choosing several from the option set; 'tags' for free creation of new entries alongside the option set.

placeholder.description: Guidance text shown inside the control before any value is chosen, communicating what the field is selecting.

softRules: Prefer the structured options prop over declarative <Select.Option> children so the dataset stays data-driven and serializable.
Pair every Select with a visible label (via antd.form.Item label or aria-label) — the placeholder alone is not an accessible name.
For filtering intents, set optionFilterProp and a sensible default value so the control is immediately useful.
When the option list is long, enable showSearch so users can find an entry rather than scrolling.
Do not co-locate destructive actions inside a Select; selection commits a value, not an action.

semantics.multiple: User may choose more than one option from the set; value is an array.
semantics.single: Exactly one option may be chosen at a time; value is a scalar.
semantics.tags: User may choose existing options and also create new free-text entries; value is an array of strings.
